regime: Risk-Off Continues, Gold Rotates Higher (Equities Day 4, Crude Cracks)
summary: Risk-off rolled into a new month, but it stopped treating every board the same. The Nasdaq fell a fourth straight day, off 1.43 percent to 28,138.50, and the S&P slipped 0.50 percent to 7,576.25, both pinned under their trend stops. Crude was the real damage, down 6.92 percent to 95.85 as the multi-day de-risk finally reached it and broke its stop hard. Gold went the other way. It bounced 1.83 percent to 3,955.60, reclaimed its stop and flipped long, the only board higher and the first haven bid of this selloff. VIX pushed up about 10 percent to 21.28, so fear is still bid, but money rotated into gold and out of crude.

setups.stop: Short while below: MNQ 28,495, MES 7,634, crude 98.28. Gold is above its 3,932 stop, so long there.

setups.bias: The indexes and crude closed below their ATR stops and trend down; December gold reclaimed its stop and flipped long, the only board higher. Trade each board on its own signal, not a blanket thesis.

setups.bias: MNQ broke the opening range down at 17:18 UTC and closed below it and below NYVWAP, the clean short-only hand-off. HOF is eligible Tuesday.

setups.name: AVWAP Bounce
setups.entry: Short rallies that fail at AVWAP or NYVWAP while price is below the stop.
setups.stop: A full reclaim of AVWAP 28,506 and the 28,495 stop invalidates.
setups.bias: Borderline. Price is below its stop and using AVWAP and NYVWAP as resistance, the continuation read, but a fast tape makes the retest timing tricky.

event.name: No scheduled tier-one US release (federal data subject to shutdown-related delays)
event.consensus: The federal data calendar stays thin and unreliable under the shutdown backdrop, so scheduled releases were not the driver. ISM Manufacturing PMI, a private survey, would be the first November read.
event.actual: A fourth straight risk-off session for the Nasdaq, but with a rotation underneath. Equities and crude fell while December gold reversed up and reclaimed its stop as a haven bid returned.
event.surprise: Crude took the hardest hit of the de-risk, down 6.92 percent, while gold was the only board higher, up 1.83 percent. VIX pushed toward 21.28.
event.nqReaction: NQ fell 1.43 percent, broke its opening range down at 17:18 UTC, stayed below its ATR stop and EMA50, and closed 28,138.50 after a 28,101.25 low.
event.crossAsset: MES minus 0.50 percent at 7,576.25, holding above Friday's low. December gold plus 1.83 percent at 3,955.60, the only board higher. December crude minus 6.92 percent at 95.85, the worst board. VIX about 21.28, up roughly 10 percent.

risk.sizing: Defensive. The selloff is four sessions deep for the Nasdaq and just cracked crude, so no new index longs and reduced size overall.
risk.openRisk: The indexes and crude are below their ATR stops; the only long is December gold, a reversal off a hard selloff. A multi-day break can keep extending and a fresh long off the lows can fail, so keep size small and honor the stops.
risk.note: Throttle state DEFENSIVE. No drawdown flags and the daily loss budget is unused, but the selloff is now four sessions deep for the Nasdaq and just cracked crude. No new index longs. The long-only momentum edge (E3v2) is blocked with price below EMA50 and ROC negative. TSMOM can work the short side on the indexes while price stays below the stops (MNQ 28,495, MES 7,634) and on crude below 98.28. December gold flipped long above its 3,932 stop, the one new long on the board, but it is a knife-catch reversal after a hard selloff, so keep size small and honor the 3,932 stop. Keep size small overall into a fast tape with VIX at 21.28. The data calendar stays thin under the shutdown, so treat any headline as the catalyst. Daylight saving ended Nov 1, so the NY cash open is now 14:30 UTC; next policy event is the December FOMC.

psychology: The easy read today was short everything, and on the indexes and crude it worked. Gold did not get the memo. It reversed hard and flipped long while the rest of the board fell, and that is the tell. A blanket risk-off thesis is not a trade. Each instrument carries its own stop for a reason, and today three said short while gold said long. Trade the signal in front of you, not the headline you expect. When one name breaks ranks the way gold did, respect it instead of fighting it, because that is often where the next move starts.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN (MNQ)
fullReport.html:
Trend-down break that held. OR High 28,748.75, OR Low 28,639.75, Width 109 pts.

Anchored at the 14:30 UTC NY cash open (EST, after daylight saving ended Nov 1). Price poked above the range at 15:12 UTC to 28,769.5 (a failed up-break), then broke down at 17:18 UTC at 28,638.75 and stayed under the range. The 20:00 UTC cash-close bar closed 28,138.50, below the opening range and below NYVWAP 28,538.12. It is Monday with no FOMC or CPI, so all four HTA OPEN playbooks are eligible: BIR, HOF, MID and BNC. The clean short-only hand-off set up on the down break; there was no back-into-range because the close finished below the range. Volume is disclaimed on the continuous contract, so VWAP uses a typical-price mean.

Price rode the lower bands down into the close, finishing 28,138.50, just above the minus 2 sigma band at 28,116.21, about 1.9 sigma under the mean. That is a trend-day slide, not a stretched-and-reclaimed reversion. A reversion-grade signal would need a stretched touch of the minus 2 or minus 3 sigma band followed by a reclaim, which did not set up, so the reversion edge is not in habitat today.

yesterdaysMapScore.note: Published Oct 30 for the Monday Nov 2 session. Risk-off extended but rotated: three of five rows triggered, two playing out and one mixed. The MNQ down path delivered in full to a 28,101.25 low, past the 28,232 and 28,123 marks. MES broke its stop late and only partly delivered, holding above the 7,557.75 target. The two not-triggered rows were the bullish turns that happened instead: gold reclaimed its 3,930 stop and closed up 1.83 percent, and the MNQ reclaim never set up.
